This man just walked away from the world championship.
On purpose.
Japan, 1976. Final race.
He leads James Hunt by three points.
On lap two, he pulls in and climbs out.
To understand why, rewind eighty-four days.
Germany. The Nürburgring. The track drivers call the Green Hell.
Lap two. His car snaps into the barrier and bursts into flames.
Trapped in the fire until other drivers drag him out.
Burned. Lungs full of toxic smoke.
Doctors don't think he'll survive.
Forty-two days later, he's racing again.
Wounds still bleeding under his helmet. He finishes fourth.
Back to Japan.
The rain is so heavy, drivers can barely see.
He's already been through fire once.
So he parks, and walks away.
Hunt takes the title. By one point.
He said his life was worth more than a title.
The bravest thing he ever did wasn't coming back.
It was knowing when to stop.
That's why...
